findings.text: follow-on: the diff edits a file outside the node's declared write paths. The dispatch fenced reckon/crew/obligations.py, tests/test_a_sub_floor_duty_names_a_runnable_command.py, tests/test_an_unsplittable_command_has_no_action_form.py, the evidence fragment and an unused figures tree; tests/test_sub_floor_dimension_is_an_obligation.py is not among them, yet its assertion that the exemption word appears in row['next_command'] was repointed at row['exempt_alternative']. The edit is one line, is required for the head gate to stay green (the contract change makes the old assertion false), is disclosed in the run manifest's changed_paths and in the fragment, and no concurrent node's declared scope names the file, so nothing collided and the landed state is correct. It should still be covered by a recorded scope extension, because the fence is exclusive and this is the shape the stop rule names as a blocker to report rather than absorb.

follow-on: the newly added exempt_alternative field is produced on the sub-floor duty row (reckon/crew/obligations.py:1184) but read by no production surface. The coordinator checklist renders only next_command, so the exemption shape that the old prose carried inline ('or exempted with the recorded reason') no longer appears on the line a coordinator reads; it survives only in the crew(view='obligations') JSON payload, which spreads the rows verbatim at reckon/mcp_views.py:3824. The placement is what the brief directed, so this is a consequence rather than a deviation, but the human-facing surface lost an option it used to show.

follow-on: assert row['next_action_form'] == rendered compares the reader's stored form against a fresh call to the same function on the same input, so the two sides move together and the line cannot fail once the rendering assertions at lines 168-172 hold. It is redundant rather than load-bearing: durability does not rest on it, because the negative control shows lines 140, 154 and 168 redden when the prose command is restored (4 failed, EXIT=1 at af2fb34e), and the assertion at line 173 is the one that pins the reader's own storage.

item_verdicts.goal: The goal is to make the sub-floor duty carry a runnable crew dispose command in next_command in place of prose, as the brief names. The landed composer builds 'reckon crew dispose --project <project> --run <run_id> --dimension <dimension> --kind folded --node \'<the node the finding went into>\'' with every value shlex.quote'd, and the exemption shape rides beside it in a new exempt_alternative field. Every option it emits exists on the CLI it names: --project, --run (reviewed_run_id), --dimension, --kind, --node and --reason are all declared on crew dispose in reckon/crew_run_commands.py:564-608, and the dispose action is a declared crew write action in reckon/mcp_crew_actions.py:33. The goal is met.
